findings: Neither pair nor scan defining module defines a total outcome-state accessor or resume. Existing native Demand.Outcome.state/resume concern a different outcome type.

One public five-tag full pair-State projection in a new module is a justified minimal boundary. The projection needs no equality instance; step/execute retain the two existing inline equality instances.

All actual pair memo-only branches preserve checked by record projection, including arbitrary pending handles and all absent/evaluate/busy/ready observations. They need no Valid, Good, Stable, success or new counter premise.
The native branch uses public H36 step_mono at the same Control Edge and checked state, then forwards the actual state of every yielded/done/failed/constraintError/blocked outcome.
Execute fuel induction must generalize the complete actual control and state. Only the actual yielded next/after branch uses the predecessor IH. Terminal outcomes retain their exact after state.
Public miss_readback is conditional on Valid, both misses and observed completion. None of its private helpers is needed or available to this route.

A separate later scan bound can project every exact pair after state. The candidate-first/pivot-second conditions affect residual control, not the state projection. No existing Scan.resume theorem is available.
H23 integration must use its supplied finite scan states and exact checked execute2 rebuild or public run_next. An uncorrelated rerun is excluded.
Grows preserves tables and record maps. Kernel.Extension adds issued/domain table preservation. Neither supplies a node-counter order from source to the supplied before state.
The prospective90-125 ordinary-line pair module, including its public projection, is credible under a proposed hard160. This is a planning estimate, not an approved declaration/body budget.
